'''''Sphagneticola''''' is a [[genus]] of [[flowering plant]]s in the family [[Asteraceae]].<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/28790789#page/54/mode/1up Hoffmann, Karl August Otto. 1900.  Notizblatt des Königlichen botanischen Gartens und Museums zu Berlin 3(22): 36] in Latin</ref><ref>[http://www.tropicos.org/Name/40003327 Tropicos, ''Sphagneticola'' O. Hoffm.]</ref><ref>Pruski, J.F. & G. Sancho. 2004. Asteraceae or Compositae (Aster or Sunflower Family). 33–39. In N. Smith et al. (eds.) Flowering Plants of the Neotropics. Princeton University Press, Princeton</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=130944 Flora of China, Vol. 20-21 Page 870 <big>蟛蜞菊属</big> peng qi ju shu ''Sphagneticola'' O. Hoffmann, Notizbl. Königl. Bot. Gart. Berlin. 3: 36. 1900. ]</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=130944 Flora of North America, Sphagneticola O. Hoffmann]</ref> '''Creeping-oxeye''' is a common name for plants in this genus.<ref>{{PLANTS|id=SPHAG3|taxon=Sphagneticola|accessdate=25 November 2015}}</ref>

; Species
* ''[[Sphagneticola brachycarpa]]'' <small>(Baker) Pruski</small> - Guyana, Venezuela, Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina, Peru, Bolivia
* ''[[Sphagneticola calendulacea]]'' <small> (L.) Pruski</small> - China, Japan, India, Sri Lanka, Indochina, Indonesia, Philippines
* ''[[Sphagneticola gracilis]]'' <small> (Rich.) Pruski</small> - Puerto Rico, Cuba, Hispaniola, Jamaica, Antigua<ref>[http://www.tropicos.org/Name/50084452?tab=specimens Tropicos, specimen list for ''Sphagneticola gracilis'' ]</ref>
* ''[[Sphagneticola trilobata]]'' <small>(L.) Pruski</small> - native to South America, widely naturalized in many subtropical and tropical regions (Asia, Australia, Pacific Islands, Mesoamerica, West Indies, Florida, Louisiana etc.)
* ''[[Sphagneticola ulei]]'' <small>O.Hoffm.</small> - native to the American tropics
